raw_case_text:
A 60-year-old woman, hailing from the eastern state of Uttar Pradesh in India presented to us with six- week history of high grade continuous fever associated with chills, rigors, anorexia, malaise, joint pains, and severe lethargy. The patient also stated that she noticed crops of round, raised lesions that started on her left upper limb, progressing to the right upper limb and eventually involving the whole face, upper back, and the chest and upper abdominal region, closely associated with the febrile episodes. Some of these lesions progressed to increase in size, became more nodular, and developed sunken centers that drained pus-like material, associated with pain and redness. The patient developed jaundice one week preceding her admission to our center which was associated with mild to moderate upper quadrant abdominal pain. There was no history of pruritis, pale-colored stools, or bleeding diathesis. The patient also developed swelling of the legs, which was nonpainful, not associated with facial puffiness, and not in lieu with decrement in urine output. This was associated with painful red eyes and nodular lesions over the eye lids and in the conjunctiva of the eyes associated with decreased vision. She is a teetotaler with no known comorbidities in the past or at the present and has not been consuming over the counter medications and/or complementary and alternative medications with/without steroid combinations or on any other potentially immunosuppressive medications.
On examination, the patient was found to have a temperature of 100.8 F. Her blood pressure was 128/88 mm of Hg in the right brachial region in supine position and the heart rate was 100 per minute. Pallor was evident; there was an icteric tinge without clubbing, lymphadenopathy, or cyanosis. There was bilateral pedal, pitting, nontender, and symmetrical edema. The skin examination revealed the presence of multiple crops of nodular, noduloulcerative, and papular lesions, dispersed throughout the body surface, mostly segregated to the face and upper back. These lesions were shiny and without skin changes and a few of them showed pus drainage from the central sunken areas (Figure 1). The eye examination revealed the presence of nodular lesions over the eyes and conjunctiva associated with conjunctival suffusion. The abdominal examination revealed the presence of hepatosplenomegaly and no free fluid in the abdomen. The rest of the systemic examination was essentially normal.
The blood investigations revealed the presence of hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dL (normal 12 to 15), a total leucocyte count of 5600 per cubic millimeter (normal 4000 to 10000), platelet count of 80000 lakhs per cubic millimeter (1.5 lakhs to 4.5), and an ESR of 80 (normal 0-2) with normocytic normochromic anemia. Her liver function tests revealed a total bilirubin of 3.2 mg/dL (normal 0.3 to 1.2), of which the direct fraction was 1.8 mg/dL (normal 0.2), the aspartate aminotransferase level was 50 IU/L (normal 5-40), alanine aminotransferase was 60 IU/L (7-35), alkaline phosphatase was 221 IU/L (normal 32-92), and gamma glutamyl transpeptidase was 150 IU/L (normal 7 to 64) with albumin value of 1.9 g/dL (normal 3.2 to 4.6) and INR of 1.3. The serum IgG levels were 22.6 g/L (normal 6.39 to 13.49). HIV 1 and 2, HBsAg, and anti-HCV were negative and an abdominal imaging revealed the presence of only hepatosplenomegaly without ascites or intrahepatic biliary radical dilatation and absence of abdominal lymphadenopathy. A fundoscopy performed at the bedside revealed features of uveitis and small retinal hemorrhages. The imaging of the chest was within normal limits. The patient underwent a skin biopsy from the largest lesion at the back; a percutaneous ultrasound guided liver biopsy was also done and a subsequent bone marrow study was also undertaken. The findings of the skin biopsy suggested the presence of thinned out epidermis. The dermis showed loss of adnexal structures and a rich collection of histiocytes filled with amastigote forms of leishmaniasis (Figure 2(a)). The liver biopsy revealed the presence of acinar disarray with hepatocytes showing ballooning degeneration, mild steatosis, and glycogenated nuclei. Several foci of lobular inflammation and prominence of hyperplastic Kupffer cells were noted with formation of few small granulomas. The hyperplastic Kupffer cells and granulomatous collection of macrophages showed presence of intracellular LD bodies (Figure 2(b)) which was also subsequently shown in the bone marrow biopsy (Figure 3). The patient was then finally diagnosed as a case of disseminated mucocutaneous-cutaneous leishmaniasis with concurrent ocular, hepatic, and simultaneous bone marrow involvement. She was started on antileishmanial therapy with liposomal amphotericin B at a dose of 3 mg/kg body weight from days 1 to 10 and oral Miltefosine of 100 mg per day for the next 28 days. The laboratory parameters subsequently normalized and the patient's visual acuity and other symptoms improved substantially during the rest of her hospital stay. She was discharged eventually in a stable condition, being afebrile, and is currently on regular follow up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 60-year-old female presented with a 6-week history of continuous high fevers, painful eruptive skin nodules draining pus, jaundice, and painful red eyes with decreased vision.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed continuous high-grade fevers with chills, rigors, anorexia, severe arthralgias, and profound lethargy 6 weeks prior to admission. Concurrently, eruptive crops of erythematous papules and nodules appeared on her left arm, spreading to her right arm, face, upper back, and torso; several lesions enlarged, developed necrotic sunken centers, and drained purulent material. One week prior, she developed scleral jaundice, right upper quadrant abdominal pain, bilateral leg swelling, and painful red eyes with ocular nodular eruptions and diminished visual acuity.
subjective.past_medical_history: Teetotaler with no prior medical comorbidities, chronic illnesses, or use of immunosuppressive/over-the-counter medications. Epidemiological history: resident of Uttar Pradesh, India.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports high fevers, rigors, anorexia, diffuse arthralgias, generalized fatigue, right upper quadrant discomfort, lower extremity swelling, painful red eyes, and impaired vision; denies pruritus, acholic stools, or abnormal bleeding.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature: 100.8 °F (38.2 °C), blood pressure: 128/88 mmHg, heart rate: 100 beats/min. Pallor and mild scleral icterus present; bilateral pedal pitting symmetrical edema. Dermatologic: multiple widespread crops of shiny papular, nodular, and noduloulcerative lesions with central crateriform purulent drainage, predominantly over the face and upper back. Ophthalmic: nodular lesions over eyelids and bulbar conjunctiva with conjunctival suffusion; bedside fundoscopy revealed anterior uveitis and flame-shaped retinal hemorrhages. Abdomen: hepatosplenomegaly palpable; no ascites.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin: 10.5 g/dL, total leukocyte count: 5,600/mm^3, platelet count: 80,000/mm^3, ESR: 80 mm/h. Total bilirubin: 3.2 mg/dL (direct bilirubin: 1.8 mg/dL), AST: 50 IU/L, ALT: 60 IU/L, alkaline phosphatase: 221 IU/L, GGT: 150 IU/L, serum albumin: 1.9 g/dL, INR: 1.3. Serum IgG: 22.6 g/L. Viral serologies: HIV-1/2, HBsAg, and anti-HCV all negative. Chest radiograph: normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal ultrasound: hepatosplenomegaly without ascites, biliary ductal dilatation, or lymphadenopathy. Skin punch biopsy: epidermal thinning, loss of skin adnexa, and dense dermal infiltrate of histiocytes containing intracellular microorganisms. Percutaneous liver biopsy: hepatic lobular inflammation, ballooning degeneration, mild steatosis, and hyperplastic Kupffer cells forming microgranulomas with intracellular organisms. Bone marrow aspirate: hypercellular marrow with intracellular organisms within macrophages.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmation: Histopathologic analysis of skin biopsy, liver biopsy, and bone marrow aspirate consistently demonstrated abundant intracellular Leishmania amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies) within histiocytes and hyperplastic Kupffer cells, establishing disseminated visceral and mucocutaneous leishmaniasis with multi-organ involvement (cutaneous, ocular/uveitis, hepatic, and hematologic). Viral hepatitis, HIV, and hematologic malignancies were ruled out. Management and Outcome: Treated with intravenous liposomal amphotericin B at 3 mg/kg/day on days 1 to 10, combined with oral miltefosine 100 mg daily for 28 days. The patient experienced defervescence, complete normalization of hepatic enzymes and hematologic parameters, substantial recovery of visual acuity, and regression of skin and ocular nodules, and was discharged in stable condition.
